problem: The shunt impedance is written as 1/(2πfC) where f was defined as the supply frequency. The ripple that the capacitor must bypass sits at the ripple frequency, which is 2f (100 Hz for a 50 Hz full-wave supply) and f for half-wave. A student may plug in 50 Hz and get a wrong impedance.
fix: Write: its shunt impedance at the ripple frequency f_r is 1/(2πf_r C), where f_r = 2f for full-wave and f_r = f for half-wave.

problem: The sentence 'This charge-discharge cycle repeats at f: twice per cycle for full-wave, once per cycle for half-wave' is ambiguous: for full-wave the recharge happens twice every supply cycle, so the cycle repeats at 2f, not at f.
fix: The capacitor is recharged once every half cycle in full-wave and once every full cycle in half-wave. So the charge-discharge cycle repeats at 2f for full-wave and at f for half-wave.

problem: The figure labels the discharge path 'through RL' while the text, formulas and worked example all use R for the load resistance. Two symbols for one quantity.
fix: Change the note to 'through R' so the symbol matches the rest of the chapter.
